nodes.title: OpenAI Agents SDK reference: mcp server
pydantic-ai PR 3494: FallbackModel falls back on all model API errors

nodes.text: Pydantic-AI FallbackModel default fallback_on is (ModelAPIError,): it falls to the next model on every API error (429, 5xx, connection, timeout and also 4xx rejected requests/bad credentials), not only HTTP status errors; validation errors do not trigger fallback. Hypothesis H6 ('only ModelHTTPError') is outdated: merged Nov 2025.
nodes.limitations: Docs and source read via fetch tool extracts; fallback_on is customizable so permanent-error exclusion needs a custom predicate.

nodes.text: Pydantic-AI has no retry at the HTTP transport unless a retrying transport is installed; provider SDKs retry by default (3 attempts OpenAI/Anthropic/Groq, 1 Google/Mistral/HF, 5 Bedrock); retry layers multiply; FallbackModel walks models inside a single attempt and never re-attempts the same model. AsyncTenacityTransport is deprecated (removed in v3) in favour of SDK-level retries.

LangGraph RetryPolicy defaults: initial_interval 0.5 s, backoff 2.0, max_interval 128 s, max_attempts 3 (including first), jitter on; default_retry_on retries ConnectionError and 5xx (httpx/requests) and excludes ValueError, TypeError, ArithmeticError, ImportError, LookupError, NameError, SyntaxError, RuntimeError, ReferenceError, StopIteration, OSError; any other exception is retried. It does not classify 4xx explicitly (non-5xx HTTPStatusError falls to the generic True branch is not verified).
nodes.limitations: Fetch tool paraphrased default_retry_on; exact handling of 4xx HTTPStatusError not verified.

nodes.text: LangChain with_fallbacks defaults to exceptions_to_handle=(Exception,), so it falls through on every error including permanent ones unless narrowed; separately, chat model max_retries retries network errors, 429 and 5xx but not 401/404 (OpenAI/Anthropic 2 retries, Google 6).

OpenAI Agents SDK retries are opt-in and runtime-only, with composable policies (network_error, http_status, provider_suggested, retry_after); replay is blocked when unsafe (streamed output started, stateful follow-ups with unknown safety); ModelSettings.timeout bounds each attempt. The models page documents no fallback model chain.
nodes.limitations: Absence of fallback is from one docs page only.

nodes.text: MCP timeouts: Pydantic-AI's current MCP toolset (mcp.py) has init_timeout default 5 s (connection plus initialize handshake) and read_timeout default 5 min; the Agents SDK has client_session_timeout_seconds default 5 (the ClientSession read timeout, i.e. per request, not documented as a separate startup timeout; None/0 disables). H7's '5 s default' holds for both, but they mean different things.
nodes.limitations: MCPServerStdio class in pydantic-ai was not read (extract covered MCPToolset only); Agents SDK page read only first 100k chars.

nodes.text: Cleanup designs: Pydantic-AI's MCP class builds an AsyncExitStack in __aenter__, commits with pop_all(), refcounts nested enters (_running_count) and closes only at zero, with a shutdown grace period; the Agents SDK MCPServerManager keeps connect and cleanup on the same task (worker task per server when connect_in_parallel), cleans up servers in reverse order, and recommends drop_failed_servers=True.

Cross-task cancel-scope errors ('Attempted to exit cancel scope in a different task than it was entered in') from anyio affect MCP stdio clients when enter and exit happen in different tasks (pools, GC finalizers, background cleanup); seen in langchain-mcp-adapters, FastMCP, Google ADK, deer-flow. Evidence is from search snippets only; no pydantic-ai or Agents SDK issue was found.

Fetch the primary GitHub issues for the anyio cancel-scope bug (langchain-mcp-adapters #99, fastmcp #348, python-sdk) and the MCP Python SDK stdio_client shutdown sequence (stdin close, terminate, kill timeouts); verify orphan-subprocess behavior.

Core should own one transient/permanent classifier (timeout, connection, 429, 5xx, overloaded = transient; 400, 401/403, 404, context-length = permanent). Retry only transient errors in one layer (set SDK max_retries to 0 or own it, not both). The fallback chain should move on transient errors and provider-side permanent errors (auth, model not found) but not on caller errors (400 bad request, context length), by passing an explicit predicate rather than the permissive library defaults.

MCP lifecycle: wrap each server startup in an explicit timeout (init handshake about 5 s), set a separate per-call timeout, own each client in one dedicated task or an AsyncExitStack entered and exited by the same task, clean up in reverse order, and drop failed servers instead of failing the host.
